sampling_model.design: An i.i.d. observational sample augmented by deterministic public nuisance functions \((m_0,m_1,p)\), supplied global \(L^2(P_X)\) error radii bounded by the fixed cap \(\bar r\), a fixed signal envelope \(E_P[(g_1(X)-g_0(X))^2]\le M\), and decision rules that may use all public inputs.
sampling_model.units: Independent units \(O_i=(Y_i,D_i,X_i)\), \(i=1,\ldots,n\), from a causal law satisfying consistency and conditional ignorability.
sampling_model.treatment: Binary treatment with propensity \(e(X)\), positive almost surely and allowed to approach zero.
sampling_model.overlap: Uniform one-sided dyadic shells satisfy \(c_-u^{\kappa}\le P\{u/2<e(X)\le u\}\le c_+u^{\kappa}\) for \(0<u\le\lambda_0\), while \(e(X)\le1-\eta_+\).
sampling_model.nuisance_estimation: The minimax infima range over rules measurable in \(O^{(n)}\) that also receive the supplied \(m_0\), \(m_1\), \(p\), \(r_{0n}\), \(r_{1n}\), and \(r_{en}\). The same public inputs are held fixed throughout each lower family, and the certified radii lie in \([0,\bar r]\).

comparator_promise_table.comparator_claim: Theorem 1 gives a squared quantile-minimax WATE lower bound in the paper's estimator-bounded class; for constant weight, the interpretive squared-radius mapping yields \(n^{-1/2}+\max\{r_{0n},r_{1n}\}r_{en}\), while Remark 2 retains the treated-side lower-bound form with known baseline response.

Section 2 gives the lower-rate form \(n^{-1/2}+\varepsilon_n\delta_n\) for one mean functional in its pure structure-agnostic class; the analogous control-arm statement remains armwise and is not a joint ATE equivalence.
Thresholded AIPW is uniformly asymptotically normal under sufficient weak-overlap nuisance conditions.
IPW has Gaussian or stable limits according to tail and trimming regimes.
Extreme propensity scores generate non-Gaussian limit theory for IPW and doubly robust estimators.
Localized fuzzy hypotheses yield a minimax lower bound for pointwise CATE.
Inverse-weight estimation can have tail-dependent irregular rates.
Limited-overlap confidence accuracy is driven by local comparison-cell sizes.
Section 6.1 treats bounded-overlap ATE examples, while the conclusion identifies weak-overlap distribution shift as an open extension.

Theorem 3.1 gives asymptotic linearity and a studentized Gaussian limit for bias-corrected trimmed doubly robust estimators targeting the original treatment-effect estimand, with Proposition B.1 verifying the ATE specialization.

body.tldr: Global prediction accuracy does not determine the attainable accuracy of the population ATE once treated observations become polynomially rare. In a public-function experiment with fixed, bounded global \(L^2(P_X)\) certificates, a fixed \(L^2(P_X)\) envelope for the conditional treatment-effect signal, and uniform one-sided propensity shells, the proposed theorem identifies a four-channel frontier \(\rho_n\): tail-amplified outcome noise, regression error hidden in shells with no treated observations, localized propensity--treated-regression uncertainty, and the regular control-side nuisance interaction. The minimax decision class consists of measurable rules using the sample, public functions, and certified radii. A clipped doubly robust average attains absolute and fixed-probability risk, a five-block median attains root mean-squared risk, and a bias-aware interval has matching honest expected length. The open sequel asks for the exact cost of adapting to unknown shell and nuisance certificates.

project_justification.gap: Regular-setting structure-agnostic results supply useful nuisance-product lower-bound templates, but the cited statements do not establish a joint two-arm minimax equivalence for \(\mathcal M_n^{\mathrm{reg}}\). Weak-overlap papers give trimming rules, irregular limits, or sufficient Wald conditions. MaSantAnnaSasakiUra2026DRWeakOverlap, Theorem 3.1 and Proposition B.1, is especially close on target preservation: its bias-corrected trimmed doubly robust method retains the original ATE and yields asymptotic inference, but it does not characterize global-\(L^2\) public-function minimax risk or the matching lower bound for expected honest-set length. None of the opened papers jointly characterizes minimax absolute risk, root mean-squared risk, fixed-probability error, and expected honest-set length for the same full-population ATE under bounded global prediction-error certificates, a fixed conditional-effect signal envelope, an explicit public-information decision class, and uniform one-sided shells.
project_justification.niche: The public-function model separates what a learner knows globally from where treated observations actually occur. A fixed bound \(E_P[(g_1(X)-g_0(X))^2]\le M\) makes the ATE functional finite without imposing a pointwise or armwise outcome envelope. The left tail generates three treated-side obstructions with different scales, while the control-side product channel remains regular.
project_justification.fill: The core supplies an explicit public-information decision class, bounded nuisance radii, a fixed treatment-effect signal moment envelope, one clipped estimator, median amplification, and four fixed-sign-valid converse channels. The repaired control-product channel is constructed on a fixed band of the perturbable active tail reservoir, where positivity, right overlap, both dyadic shell inequalities, nuisance membership, collision control, and exact mixture cancellation are verified before it is combined with the other channels. The polynomial deterioration threshold and an oracle bias-aware interval are indexed by \(\rho_n\).

body.related_work: JinSyrgkanis2024StructureAgnosticDR, Theorem 1, gives a squared quantile-minimax WATE lower bound in its own estimator-bounded class. With constant weight and the interpretive substitutions \(e_n=r_{0n}^2\), \(e_n'=r_{1n}^2\), and \(f_n=r_{en}^2\), its square-root lower-bound scale has form \(n^{-1/2}+\max\{r_{0n},r_{1n}\}r_{en}\); Remark 2 retains the treated-side \(n^{-1/2}+r_{1n}r_{en}\) form with known baseline response. These source results inform the dyadic-reservoir converse, but they are not an equivalence theorem for \(\mathcal M_n^{\mathrm{reg}}\). BonviniKennedyDukesBalakrishnan2024StructureAgnosticATE, Section 2, states that no estimator of its single mean functional \(\psi\) over its pure structure-agnostic class is faster than \(n^{-1/2}+\varepsilon_n\delta_n\). The paper notes an analogous control-arm result, but this remains armwise and does not itself establish a joint two-arm ATE minimax equivalence or matching upper bound for the comparator class in this note. The shell class is disjoint from \(\mathcal M_n^{\mathrm{reg}}\); the fast-tail limit of \(\rho_n\) has the same parametric-plus-product algebraic form as these lower-bound templates after radius identification, which is only a sanity comparison and not a class-inclusion transfer. JinSyrgkanis2025GeneralLinearFunctionalLowerBounds, Section 6.1 and the conclusion, broadens structure-agnostic lower bounds while retaining bounded-overlap ATE examples and expressly identifies weak-overlap distribution shift as open; it supplies the regime-opening anchor rather than a theorem matched here. Dorn2025WeakOverlapTStatistics gives a clipped cross-fitted AIPW Gaussian limit under sufficient tail and nuisance conditions; it informs the upper score but is not a risk comparator. MaSantAnnaSasakiUra2026DRWeakOverlap, Theorem 3.1 and Proposition B.1, constructs a bias-corrected trimmed doubly robust estimator that preserves the original ATE and establishes asymptotic linearity and normal inference; it does not give the global-\(L^2\) public-function minimax-risk frontier or the matching honest-length converse. MaWang2020RobustIPW derives Gaussian and stable IPW limits and selects a trimming threshold from the sample for its own IPW criterion. HeilerKazak2021ExtremePropensity develops non-Gaussian limit theory for IPW and doubly robust estimators under extreme propensity scores. Those limit-law results address irregular inference, whereas the present result matches global-\(L^2\) minimax absolute risk, root mean-squared risk, fixed-probability error, and honest expected length. KennedyBalakrishnanRobinsWasserman2024MinimaxCATE provides the localized fuzzy-hypothesis method for a different estimand and smoothness class. KhanTamer2010Irregular explains why support tails govern inverse-weight rates. Rothe2017RobustCI motivates local effective sample size and limited-overlap coverage, but its robust intervals rely on finite-cell or auxiliary distributional structure rather than the four-channel global-\(L^2\) radius.
body.technical_internal_limitation: The lower frontier is restricted to reservoir-rich fixed shell constants satisfying ass:lower-shell-richness and ass:upper-shell-richness. Each lower family calibrates its regression perturbation to satisfy ass:bounded-treatment-effect-signal. In the repaired control-product family, the perturbation is supported on the fixed active-reservoir band \(B=\{s_c<e_0\le2s_c\}\): every fixed sign has propensity ratio in \([3/4,5/4]\), preserves positivity and right overlap, consumes at most half of the shell slack \(\Delta=c_+-2^\kappa c_-\), and obeys both global \(L^2(P_X)\) certificates. The upper bound needs only uniform shells and the fixed signal moment, so arbitrarily tight admissible shell constants may have a different converse geometry.
body.honest_scope: The main theorem treats supplied public functions, bounded certified radii, fixed shell constants, and the primitive signal condition \(E_P[(g_1(X)-g_0(X))^2]\le M\); it imposes no stronger pointwise or armwise potential-outcome envelope and makes no Wald or asymptotic-normality claim. The minimax rules may use every supplied public input. Adaptation to unknown calibration, bounded-outcome variants, arbitrary shell constants, and the exact studentized-validity region remain open. The dyadic-shell and bounded-overlap classes share the signal condition but are distinct. The fast-tail analytic limit is \((1+r_{1n})n^{-1/2}+r_{1n}r_{en}+r_{0n}r_{en}\), uniformly equivalent to \(n^{-1/2}+r_{1n}r_{en}+r_{0n}r_{en}\) under \(r_{1n}\le\bar r\); this is the same algebraic form as the cited lower-bound templates after radius identification, not a minimax equivalence theorem for \(\mathcal M_n^{\mathrm{reg}}\).
body.interpretation: The regular-benchmark reduction is an internal check on the four-channel formula: as \(\kappa\to\infty\), its rate has the same parametric-plus-product algebraic form obtained from the cited lower-bound templates after an explicit radius identification. Because those citations use their own source classes and lower-bound risk conventions, this comparison does not identify the minimax risk on \(\mathcal M_n^{\mathrm{reg}}\), does not supply a matching regular-class upper bound, and does not transfer results by class inclusion.
